packs.title: Lines in the Light
packs.promise: Follow Barcelona’s curves, textures and small surprises into a story of your own.

q.s: Find three kinds of delicacy in a huge stone facade.
st: Choose a comfortable public-square view of the Cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulàlia from Pla de la Seu. No stairs or entry are required.
Find a pointed arch, a repeated narrow opening and one small carved edge that catches light.
Compare the solid wall with the spaces between its details. Which part feels lightest?
Save the three finds and one sentence about that lightness.

q.s: Build a quiet three-shape composition from a basilica’s exterior.
st: From the public square, look at the front of Santa Maria del Mar, the Gothic basilica in La Ribera. Do not enter or join a tour.
Choose a circle, an upright line and a pointed shape from the facade. The rose window can be observed as a shape without seeing its small details.
Arrange those three shapes into a small imagined design: a sketch, a pattern, or three lines describing it.
Give your design a title and save it quietly.

q.s: Find stone, glass and ceramic doing different jobs.
st: Use a clear public-pavement view of Casa Batlló at Passeig de Gràcia 43. No ticket, entrance queue or rooftop visit is part of this mission.
Find a stone curve, a glass reflection and a ceramic colour patch. A distant observation or official close-up is enough.
Describe each material with one texture word based on what you see. Do not touch the facade.
Save the three material-and-word pairs and choose the one you noticed last.

packs.title: Hill and Horizon
packs.promise: Explore Montjuïc through garden details, architectural forms and a port-side pause.

q.s: Turn a pavilion’s material contrast into a small design.
st: Choose a booked pavilion visit during its current opening, or use the official photographs without buying a ticket. Follow visitor barriers; the pool is for looking, not touching.
Find one flat stone plane and one reflection or transparent surface. Describe the difference between the two; a photograph inside is unnecessary.
Make a small two-part design using a solid shape and a lighter outline. Change one part and note how the contrast changes.
Follow an open garden path to a comfortable viewing position. Stay away from water edges and do not pick plants.
Find a leaf outline, a planted-bed edge and a contrast between two surfaces. Use what is visible today; flowers and pond reflections are optional.
Save the three observations in words or sketches. Add one question about a plant or shape rather than guessing its name.

q.s: Make a small design from a distinctive tower silhouette.
st: Use an open public viewpoint or the tourism authority’s tower photograph. Stay outside barriers around the structure.
Find the leaning white shaft, the arc held near its top and the tall thin element above. Simplify them into three lines or shapes.
Make a second tiny design by changing just the arc. Describe what that change does to the balance; your design is not an engineering explanation.
